# Research notes: Labour minus National seat margin, 2026 NZ general election (as of 2026-09-28)

The election is on 7 Nov 2026, so nothing has resolved yet. The latest poll (1News–Verian, 23–27 Sep) has Labour and National tied at 28% and 34 seats each, a margin of 0.

## 1. Resolution source and timing
- **Election date:** Saturday 7 Nov 2026. The Electoral Commission release of 21 Jan 2026 says: "The 2026 General Election will be held on Saturday 7 November 2026." https://elections.nz/media-and-news/2026/key-dates-for-2026-general-election
- **Scheduled dates before resolution:**
  - Writ day 4 Oct; nominations close 8 Oct.
  - Enrolment closes 25 Oct; advance voting starts 26 Oct. I haven't checked either date on the source page.
  - Preliminary results from 7pm on 7 Nov at electionresults.govt.nz.
  - **Official results declared 27 Nov 2026.**
  - Writ returned by 3 Dec.
- **Which count decides it:** the question says "seats won" but doesn't say whether that means preliminary or official. Special votes have moved the margin by 1–3 seats in Labour's favour (see section 3), so this could matter.
- **Parliament size:** 120 seats plus any overhang. The 2023 election produced 123 (Wikipedia).
- **Baseline:**
  - 2023 official result: National 48, Labour 34, a margin of −14.
  - Current parliament: National 49 after the Port Waikato by-election, Labour 34, a margin of −15. Source is Wikipedia and is uncertain: the same page also says the total is 122 after Judith Collins resigned in May 2026. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/54th_New_Zealand_Parliament
  - These are pre-election seat counts and don't count toward resolution.

## 3. Base rates (MMP elections 1996–2023, official results)
Margin is Labour seats minus National seats.

| Year | Margin | Lab / Nat seats |
|---|---|---|
| 1996 | −7 | 37 / 44 |
| 1999 | +10 | 49 / 39 |
| 2002 | +25 | 52 / 27 |
| 2005 | +2 | 50 / 48 |
| 2008 | −15 | 43 / 58 |
| 2011 | −25 | 34 / 59 |
| 2014 | −28 | 32 / 60 |
| 2017 | −10 | 46 / 56 |
| 2020 | +32 | 65 / 33 |
| 2023 | −14 | 34 / 48 |

- **Range:** −28 to +32. Labour won more seats in 4 of 10 elections.
- **Closest precedent for a near-tie:** 2005 (+2), when the parties were 2 points apart on the party vote (41.1 vs 39.1).
- **Scale:** roughly 1 point of party-vote gap equals about 1.2 seats of margin, at current levels of wasted vote. This is my rough derivation.
- **Final polls vs result:**
  - 2017: National overstated by about 1.5 points.
  - 2020: National overstated by 3–5.5 points and Labour understated by 3–4.
  - 2023: National understated by 1–4 points (7.5 in Roy Morgan) and Labour slightly overstated.
  - So the direction isn't consistent. Errors on the gap were about 2–9 points, which is roughly 2–11 seats.
- **Special votes:** National lost 1–2 seats between preliminary and official results in every election from 2005 to 2023. Specials moved the Labour−National margin toward Labour by +3 (2017), +3 (2020) and +2 (2023). Specials were 20.9% of all votes in 2023.
- **Sources:** Wikipedia election pages for 1999–2023, elections.nz official-results releases, and https://www.odt.co.nz/news/national/final-election-results-national-loses-two-labour-m%C4%81ori-party-pick-one
- **Uncertain items:** 1996 vote shares and 2011 Labour figures are from memory (they look correct). The 2008 and 2014 preliminary National counts were worked out, not seen in a source.

criterios: This question will resolve as the number of seats won by the Labour Party minus the number of seats won by the National Party in the 2026 New Zealand general election.
razonamientos:
(a) **Time left:** The election is on 7 November 2026, about 6 weeks away. Preliminary results come that night. Official results, which include special votes, are declared on 27 November, about 8.5 weeks away.

(b) **If nothing changed:** The latest 1News–Verian poll has Labour and National tied at 34 seats each, a margin of 0. The average of recent polls is roughly even, with perhaps a slight Labour edge. If the official count is used, special votes have typically moved the margin 2–3 seats toward Labour. That points to about 0 to +2.

(c) **If the current trend continued:** Both major parties are sliding while the Greens surge. Recent polls (Verian, Freshwater, Anacta) show National slipping slightly more than Labour. There is no strong directional trend between the two, so the margin would sit near 0 to +2.

(d) **Experts and markets:**
- Polymarket's seat ladders put both parties' medians around 35 seats, which implies a margin near 0. Labour's ladder has a slightly fatter upper tail.
- Kalshi, via an aggregator, has Labour about 62¢ to win the most seats. These markets are thin.
- Poll-of-polls aggregates show the two parties essentially tied, with Kiwipolls at National 37, Labour 36.

(e) **Unexpected low scenario:** The polling error repeats 2023, when National was understated by several points. Luxon also performs well in the 6 October debate, and Green gains come mainly at Labour's expense. National could then finish 8–12 seats ahead.

(f) **Unexpected high scenario:** A late collapse in coalition support, like the 2020-style polling error in Labour's favour, combined with special votes, could put Labour 10+ seats ahead.

**Summary:** Past errors on the party-vote gap between the two have been 2–9 points, and each point is worth roughly 1.2 seats. Adding possible movement during the campaign gives a standard deviation of about 7 seats around a median of about +1.
